en: The Philippine eagle (Pithecophaga jefferyi) is a large bird of prey featuring a distinctive shaggy crest and powerful, sharp talons.
The sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) is the national flower of the Philippines, known for its highly fragrant white blossoms that bloom year-round.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces by carving steps into mountains, using an ancient stone irrigation system to grow rice.
Mount Mayon in Albay is a perfectly symmetrical stratovolcano that frequently erupts due to the subduction of the Philippine Sea tectonic plate.
The Philippine carabao is a domesticated swamp buffalo scientifically adapted to thrive in the country's hot, humid climate and muddy terrains.
Filipino scientists at the International Rice Research Institute developed the IR8 high-yield rice variety to help prevent widespread famine across Asia.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain, an evolutionary adaptation that helps it hunt insects at night.
The Pahiyas Festival in Lucban celebrates the rice harvest by decorating houses with kiping, which are brightly colored, leaf-shaped wafers made from rice.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented an improvised bamboo incubator that kept premature babies warm without needing a continuous electricity supply.
Filipino adobo uses vinegar and salt as natural preservatives, which historically allowed the meat to safely last for days without refrigeration.
The South Sea pearl, produced by the Pinctada maxima oyster in Philippine waters, is the official national gem of the country.
The Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999 is a national law that regulates vehicle emissions and bans incineration to protect public health.
